meta.method: Every risk row is grounded in a verified official fact linked to data/sources.json. Likelihood (1-5) and Impact (1-5) are explicit analytical scores used to rank risk exposure across all five property decisions.

rows.risk: WALT falls below 6 years, shrinking buyer debt availability and expanding exit cap rate by 75–175 bps
rows.mechanism: Institutional net-lease portfolios maintain ~10.2-year WALT (S13). Once a 2030–2035 lease drops below 6 years remaining term, 10-year commercial loan amortization tightens and passive §1031 buyers exit the bidding pool.
rows.mitigation: Initiate early Blend-and-Extend negotiations in 2026–2027 or execute a §1031 disposition while >=5.5–6.0 years of primary term remain.

rows.risk: Tenant exercises non-renewal or 'JACK on Track' closure at 2030–2035 lease expiration
rows.mechanism: Jack in the Box system shrank by 76 net units across FY2025 (-55) and YTD Q3 FY2026 (-21), with 86 FY25 closures and 50–100 FY26 closures guided under 'JACK on Track' (S11, S12).
rows.mitigation: Audit store-level gross sales (M-07) and option notice dates (M-05) immediately; if rent-to-sales exceeds 10%, prioritize early sale before tenant non-renewal notice window.

rows.risk: Renewal reprices rent downward if current contract rent exceeds market or store sales coverage
rows.mechanism: JACK's FY2025 10-K explicitly states it renews expiring leases 'at then-current market rates' (S11), and franchise AUV declined -3.8% in FY25 ($1,874k vs $1,949k) with -4.2% YTD FY26 SSS (S11, S12).
rows.mitigation: Trade early term certainty in 2026–2027 for a contractual fixed or CPI-collared rent schedule rather than waiting for an uncollared expiry negotiation.

rows.risk: California AB 1228 $20.00/hr fast-food wage floor and $18.42/hr LA City wage compress operator EBITDA
rows.mechanism: AB 1228 raised CA fast-food minimum wage +25% to $20.00/hr (S09) while LA City's general floor rose to $18.42/hr on July 1, 2026 (S10); JACK company store margins fell from 21.7% (FY24) to 19.6% (FY25) (S11).
rows.mitigation: Underwrite tenant rent capacity at <=8.5% of gross unit sales; avoid over-leveraging or relying on aggressive rent bumps.

rows.risk: LA inflation (+3.7% All Items, +20.3% Energy YoY in Sep 2026) erodes real value of fixed NNN rent bumps
rows.mechanism: Nov 4, 2026 BLS release shows LA CPI-U at +3.7% YoY and Energy up +20.3% YoY (S01). Flat or 1.5%/yr lease escalations lose ~1.7%–2.2%/yr in real purchasing power while utility spikes strain franchisee margins.
rows.mitigation: Require CPI-linked escalators (e.g., 2.0% floor / 3.5% cap) in any lease extension or rotate via §1031 into CPI-escalating net leases.

rows.risk: Elevated 10-Year Treasury yields (4.84%–5.31%) keep net-lease cap rates wide and compress exit multiples
rows.mechanism: FRED DGS10 is 4.84% on 2026-11-05 (peak 5.31% on 2026-10-05) and FOMC upper limit is 4.00% (S15, S16), anchoring NNN REIT acquisition yields at 7.4% (S13) and Realty Income at 7.3% (S14).
rows.mitigation: Sell with long remaining term (or fresh 15-yr extension) to capture the 6.4% occupied disposition cap tier (S13) and redeploy into 7.3%–7.4% replacement assets.

rows.risk: Sale triggers 100% FMV Prop 13 reassessment, spiking NNN property tax billed directly to the tenant
rows.mechanism: Under Prop 13 (1% base levy, 2%/yr cap, 100% reassessment on sale, S17), a long-held parcel's low tax basis resets to the purchase price upon sale. In an NNN lease, that tax jump hits the tenant's occupancy cost right before renewal.
rows.mitigation: Calculate the exact Prop 13 tax jump from the current tax bill (M-09) before listing; extend the lease prior to sale so the buyer and tenant have already absorbed/agreed to post-sale occupancy costs.

rows.risk: City of LA Measure ULA confiscates 4.0% or 5.5% of gross sale proceeds if price crosses $5.4M / $10.9M
rows.mechanism: Effective July 1, 2026, City of LA levies a 4.45% total transfer tax (0.45% base + 4.0% ULA) on gross price above $5,400,000 and 5.95% at/above $10,900,000 (S18). Crossing $5.40M by $1 costs $216,000.
rows.mitigation: Verify parcel municipal boundary (M-08); if inside City of LA and valuation approaches $5.4M, cap contract price at $5.39M to avoid the $216k+ cliff.

rows.risk: Outright taxable sale loses ~28%–37% of gain to Federal LTCG (23.8%), §1250 Recapture (28.8%), and CA Tax (13.3%)
rows.mechanism: Without an IRC §1031 exchange, combined Federal (20% LTCG + 3.8% NIIT, 25% §1250 recapture) and California (up to 13.3% ordinary treatment) taxes severely reduce reinvestable principal (S19).
rows.mitigation: Execute disposition exclusively through a Qualified Intermediary under IRC §1031 (45-day ID / 180-day close) and file CA Form FTB 3840 annually if exchanging out of state (S19).

rows.risk: LA County population (-3.2% 2020–25; -2.2% projected 2025–40) and K-12 enrollment (-240,800) decline
rows.mechanism: CA DOF projects LA County population falling from 9,853,435 (2025) to 9,727,305 (2030), 9,708,647 (2035), and 9,637,524 (2040) (S04), alongside a -240,800 K-12 student decline (S05).
rows.mitigation: Rely on Central LA's high urban density (8,304.2/sq mi, S03) and healthcare/hospitality commuter traffic rather than countywide population growth; diversify geographically via §1031.

rows.risk: Information (-5.7% YoY), Financial (-1.7%), and Manufacturing (-1.2%) job losses weaken daytime office corridors
rows.mechanism: Nov 4, 2026 BLS data confirm LA metro Information employment fell -11.4k (-5.7% YoY) and Financial Activities fell -5.1k (-1.7% YoY) through Sep 2026 (S01).
rows.mitigation: Leverage Jack in the Box's 24-hour drive-thru format serving Healthcare (+3.8% YoY, +49.1k jobs) and Hospitality (+1.5% YoY) shift workers (S01).

rows.risk: 100% of property wealth tied to one parcel, one tenant brand, and one regulatory jurisdiction
rows.mechanism: Jack in the Box has 44.1% of its stores in California (941 units) and ~70% in CA+TX, explicitly flagging geographic concentration in its Form 10-K (S11).
rows.mitigation: Use a pre-cliff IRC §1031 exchange to split equity across 2–3 diversified net-lease assets in multi-state growth corridors.

rows.risk: Lease backed only by a single-unit/small franchisee LLC rather than Jack in the Box Inc.
rows.mechanism: 93% of Jack in the Box restaurants are franchised (S12), and franchisee credit trades ~75–100 bps wider than corporate credit while carrying higher default risk.
rows.mitigation: Verify guarantor entity on executed lease (M-04) and require corporate or multi-unit guaranty upon any blend-and-extend.

rows.risk: Landlord responsibility for roof/structure or $350k–$600k re-tenanting TI/LC if tenant vacates
rows.mechanism: Prototype 1,372 sq ft QSR buildings (S11) require substantial drive-thru/kitchen retrofits and 9–18 months of downtime if re-tenanted after vacancy.
rows.mitigation: Audit lease maintenance clauses (M-06) and avoid holding into the final 36 months of lease term unextended.

rows.risk: Failure to identify replacement property within 45 days or close within 180 days triggers full tax
rows.mechanism: IRS Form 8824 enforces strict, non-extendable 45-day identification and 180-day closing deadlines (S19).
rows.mitigation: Pre-underwrite three replacement properties (200% or 3-property rule) and engage Qualified Intermediary before signing PSA.

rows.risk: Subsurface soil/vapor contamination from historic urban corner use delays sale or blocks buyer financing
rows.mechanism: Older Central LA arterial corners frequently hosted mid-century auto/service stations tracked in CA GeoTracker (S26).
rows.mitigation: Run private GeoTracker lookup (M-76) and Phase I ESA prior to marketing; never authorize invasive Phase II boring without environmental counsel.

rows.risk: Major Los Angeles Basin / Puente Hills Blind-Thrust Earthquake (M>=6.7 to M>=7.5)
rows.mechanism: USGS UCERF3 establishes a 60% 30-year probability of M>=6.7, 46% of M>=7.0, and 31% of M>=7.5 in the LA region (S22); FEMA NRI ranks urban LA at the 97.8th national percentile for earthquake loss (S24). Standard NNN policies exclude earthquake, and casualty clauses often let tenants terminate.
rows.mitigation: Screen CGS liquefaction/fault zones (M-75), price commercial earthquake + rent-loss endorsement, or eliminate single-parcel seismic concentration via multi-state §1031 exchange.

rows.risk: Repeat of Jan 2025 Eaton & Palisades Fire Catastrophe Destroying Regional Infrastructure & Demand
rows.mechanism: The Jan 2025 Eaton & Palisades fires burned 37,469 acres, destroyed 16,251–16,264 structures, caused 31 fatalities, inflicted $5.2B–$10.1B in county output losses, impacted ~6,800 businesses and ~47,000 workers, and erased $900M–$1.6B in tax revenue (S21).
rows.mitigation: Verify parcel FHSZ status (M-74), confirm business-interruption/smoke/utility-shutoff insurance coverage, and maintain a 12-month liquid NOI reserve.

rows.risk: Commercial carrier withdrawal and California FAIR Plan assessment spike make NNN coverage unobtainable or punitive
rows.mechanism: CDI Order No. 2025-1 approved a historic $1.0B FAIR Plan emergency assessment after ~$4.0B in Jan 2025 wildfire claims (S23), triggering commercial policy non-renewals and surging premiums across LA County.
rows.mitigation: Audit lease insurance covenants yearly (additional insured, A-VII rating requirement) and rotate capital via §1031 into lower-insurance-friction states.

rows.risk: USGS ARkStorm West Coast Mega-Storm Overwhelming LA Basin Flood Channels
rows.mechanism: USGS ARkStorm models a ~$725B California catastrophe ($400B property + $325B business interruption) flooding up to 25% of statewide buildings and severing LA freight/power corridors (S22).
rows.mitigation: Check FEMA NFHL FIRM flood panel (M-76) and verify commercial flood and utility-interruption coverage.

rows.risk: Whole-business securitization default or Chapter 11 reorganization resulting in unilateral lease rejection
rows.mechanism: As of July 5, 2026 (Q3 FY26 10-Q, S12), JACK carries $1,472.83M of total debt and $1,008.79M of operating lease liabilities ($2.48B combined) against $46.32M unrestricted cash and a -$901.29M stockholders' deficit. Under 11 U.S.C. §365, a bankrupt tenant can reject leases and cap landlord damages.
rows.mitigation: Do not hold single-tenant JACK exposure passively through lease maturity; sell after early extension or via pre-cliff §1031 while institutional buyers still finance the brand.

rows.risk: 10-Year Treasury surges above 6.5%–7.0%, pushing QSR cap rates to 8.5%+ and freezing leveraged buyers
rows.mechanism: 10-Year Treasury already touched 5.31% in Oct 2026 (4.84% on Nov 5, 2026, S15) while LA CPI is +3.7% and Energy CPI is +20.3% (S01). A 150–200 bps rate spike cuts unlevered property value by ~20%–28%.
rows.mitigation: Avoid forced sales during the final 2–3 years of the lease; preserve zero or low parcel leverage.

rows.category: Brand Food-Safety or Franchisee Systemic Crisis
rows.risk: Systemwide foodborne illness event or multi-unit franchisee insolvency wave
rows.mechanism: JACK's FY2025 Form 10-K Risk Factors explicitly highlight food safety, supply-chain disruption, and franchisee financial distress across its 93%-franchised system (S11).
rows.mitigation: Maintain covered-land value awareness (LAMC drive-thru CUP scarcity, S20) so the pad retains re-tenanting appeal to competing QSR chains.

rows.category: Pandemic, Civil Unrest, or Extended Grid Shut-Off
rows.risk: Prolonged curfews, civil commotion, public-health dining restrictions, or PSPS power shutoffs
rows.mechanism: Urban Los Angeles tracts have a FEMA NRI Community Resilience score of only 15.4 ('Very Low', S24), and JACK's 10-K flags civil unrest and utility disruptions (S11).
rows.mitigation: Ensure lease contains strict 'hell-or-high-water' no-abatement rent language backed by 12 months of business-interruption insurance.

rows.risk: California voters pass commercial split-roll reform, eliminating Prop 13's 2%/yr assessment cap on commercial parcels
rows.mechanism: Repealing Prop 13 protection (S17) for commercial properties would trigger periodic FMV reassessment without a sale, sharply increasing NNN tenant occupancy cost or landlord carry cost.
rows.mitigation: Do not justify a long-term single-asset hold solely on Prop 13 tax lock-in; diversify via §1031 into states with predictable property tax burdens.

rows.category: Municipal Drive-Through Electrification or Ban Expansion
rows.risk: Future city air-quality/climate ordinance restricts drive-thru idling or blocks rebuild after >50% casualty
rows.mechanism: LAMC §12.24-W,17 already subjects drive-through facilities to discretionary CUP conditions (S20); losing grandfathered non-conforming status after prolonged vacancy or casualty destroys QSR pad premium.
rows.mitigation: Never allow drive-through operations to lapse beyond municipal non-conforming discontinuance windows (typically 6–12 months) during any re-tenanting.
